text:
Alex: Heads-up - noticed a bunch of customer reports about confusing 429s from the SDKs and console. They see a generic 'rate limit exceeded' and no guidance. Can we align on a better payload + console copy?

Priya: Yep, seeing same in telemetry. Most are per-org bursts that spike briefly, then clear. The SDK surfaces a generic HTTPError and Retry-After header only. Customers keep asking: is it per-key, per-org, or global?

Dana: From product POV we should make the message actionable: tell users which quota was hit, the scope (org/key), and whether a transient burst is expected. Also surface a docs link and suggested client-side backoff.

Sam: Technical note: we already compute per-key and per-org buckets server-side. We can add metadata to the 429 JSON without a big perf hit. Proposal: enrich 429 with structured fields: error.type, error.scope, error.name, error.retry_after_seconds, error.help_url and an optional quota snapshot.

Alex: Love that — can we sketch the exact JSON so SDK teams can standardize parsing? Also, let's decide on header vs body for retry info. Some SDKs only check headers.

Priya: I'd prefer body-first with a fallback header. Body has richer info (scope + quota). Include Retry-After header for old clients. So both.

Marta: I'll draft the docs copy once we have final fields. Suggested help_url: https://docs.redwood.com/api/limits#rate-limit-payloads

Sam: Draft 429 payload (example):
```json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 18
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "scope": "org",
    "name": "requests_per_minute",
    "retry_after_seconds": 18,
    "help_url": "https://docs.redwood.com/api/limits#rate-limit-payloads"
  },
  "quota_snapshot": {
    "window_seconds": "60",
    "used": "1200",
    "limit": "1000"
  }
}
```

Priya: That looks great. A couple things: quota_snapshot keys should be numbers (we'll stringify here for Slack), and we need to be careful about leaking org-wide numbers to other tenants via public logs — but within the API response to the requestor it's fine.

Dana: UX ask for console: when an admin sees repeated 429s, show a contextual banner on the dashboard: "Your org hit requests_per_minute quota. Consider enabling burst capacity or upgrading Dedicated. Learn more." Include a quick link to increase limits or request a quota review. :rotating_light:

Alex: Also add an in-console troubleshooting card with a bullet list: check which API key had errors (link to per-key telemetry), recent burst patterns, recommended backoff settings, and an option to enable temporary burst extension. Keep it small and scannable.

Sam: Implementation notes: server will add error.scope = "key|org|global"; if scope=="key" include key_id (hashed) so we can link to telemetry without exposing full key. We'll include limit_name and a numeric retry_after_seconds.

Marta: For docs I'll include SDK examples for JavaScript, Python pseudocode showing catch of RateLimit and reading body.error.retry_after_seconds then applying exponential backoff + jitter. Example snippet for JS: 
```js
try { await client.generate(...) } catch (err) {
  if (err.status === 429) {
    const r = err.body?.error?.retry_after_seconds ?? parseInt(err.headers['retry-after'], 10);
    await sleep((r || 5) * 1000 * (1 + Math.random()*0.2));
  }
}
```

Priya: We should also standardize the SDK exception type across languages (RateLimitError) and include .retryAfterSeconds, .scope, .limitName, .helpUrl fields so apps can programmatically branch (e.g., switch to a cheaper model or queue work).

Alex: Ops question: how do we surface these enriched events into the Console's alerting/telemetry? We want to correlate 429 spikes with routing policy changes / fallback activations.

Sam: We can tag each request event with quota.name and quota.scope. We'll surface aggregated counts per route/key/org in the Trace/Route dashboard and add a dedicated 'quota events' timeseries. That's a small schema change in telemetry.

Dana: For rollout UX: when we deploy the change to include the new fields, we should ship the console copy and docs at the same time so customers see actionable guidance immediately. Also add a one-week grace where console shows a 'beta' badge next to the new troubleshooting card.

Marta: I'll coordinate docs and a short console tooltip. Timeline: I can have draft docs + SDK examples by EOD Wednesday if engineering can commit to the API change in the next sprint.

Alex: Final checklist: 1) API: add structured 429 body + Retry-After header (Sam) 2) Telemetry: tag quota fields (Sam) 3) SDKs: expose RateLimitError with fields (Priya + SDK owners) 4) Console: banner + troubleshooting card + link to docs (Dana + UI) 5) Docs: examples + migration guide (Marta).

Sam: I'll open PR for the API shape and telemetry schema today. Will include migration notes and a feature flag to flip after rollout.

ops-bot: Created issue RW-5643 - "Structured 429 payloads + console UX for rate limits" assigned to @Sam. :white_check_mark:

Alex: Perfect — thanks everyone. Let's regroup in the weekly devex sync to review the PR and draft copy. :)
